patches.name: Chorus Polysynth
patches.blurb: The early-80s Japanese polysynth sound: one oscillator per voice, a fat 4-pole filter, and a bucket-brigade stereo chorus doing most of the work. Laid out as the machine's own panel, 24 faders and all.

patches.name: Warm Analog Pad
patches.blurb: Three detuned saws, a sub octave, a soft filter and a hall. The pad that sits under everything and never asks for attention.

patches.name: Glassy Bell Lead
patches.blurb: Struck metal, tuned. Inharmonic partials over an FM strike. Its sparkle control is the best macro in the set: it changes the timbre by 10 dB and the volume by none.
patches.caveat: Long decays overlap and clip near the top of the decay range. A measured defect, left in as a test case.

patches.name: Plucky FM Bass
patches.blurb: DX-style slap. Two modulators into one sine carrier, with the metallic clang living only in the attack, which is what keeps it tight instead of boomy.
patches.caveat: The width control clips at the top of its own range. A measured defect, left in as a test case.

patches.name: Acid Line
patches.blurb: A 303 in spirit. One sharp saw through a resonant ladder filter that sweeps on every note, with accent and post-filter overdrive.

patches.name: Breathy Texture
patches.blurb: Filtered noise with pitch in it, so a note reads as a colour rather than a tone. The movement is built from rates with no common period, so it never loops.
